reports.title: Decisão Normativa-TCU — coeficientes individuais de participação no Fundo de Participação dos Municípios (FPM)
reports.description: The annual normative decision fixing every Brazilian municipality's individual coefficient in the Fundo de Participação dos Municípios, the constitutional transfer under art. 159 I of the Federal Constitution. Roughly five and a half thousand municipalities, decided in one document, on a population figure and a per-capita income figure. THE FINDING SITS IN WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: across 206 pages the annexes source population twenty-eight times as "População (fonte: IBGE, ref. 01/07/2025)" — the agency and a reference date, and never a titled release. The largest funding formula in this corpus names no publication at all. What supplies the titled link is a statute and the statistical office's own compliance statement, not the formula document.
reports.cadence_note: One decision per exercise, published in November for the following year (DN-TCU 219/2025 covers exercise 2026). A parallel decision fixes the state-level FPE coefficients.

release_schedule.note: TCU issues an annual Decisão Normativa fixing individual municipal FPM coefficients for the following calendar year. Observed issuance dates cluster in mid-to-late November: DN 133/2013, 141/2014, 148/2015, 157/2016, 162/2017, 173/2019, 179/2019, 190/2020, 207/2023 (22 Nov 2023, for 2024), 213/2024 (for 2025), and 219/2025 (18 Nov 2025, for 2026). No published multi-year calendar or statutory fixed date was found specifying the exact day; the November timing is a consistent multi-year pattern rather than a stated rule. Coefficients can occasionally be altered mid-cycle by subsequent TCU decisions or court orders (e.g., STF suspensions have occurred), but the baseline annual DN follows this November pattern.

reports.title: Estimativas da População
reports.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)
reports.description: IBGE's annual resident-population estimates for every Brazilian municipality and federation unit, published in the Diário Oficial da União with a reference date of 1 July. Statutorily required, and required specifically for the transfer calculations: IBGE's own methodology note states it has published these in the DOU since 1992 in compliance with art. 102 of Lei 8.443. The reference date the TCU's annexes cite — 01/07/2025 — is this release's own.
reports.cadence_note: Annual, published by 31 August for municipalities under Lei 8.443/1992 art. 102 II; the 2025 edition was published in the DOU on 28 August 2025.

entries.covers: 2027 municipal population estimates (reference date July 1, 2027) — statutory deadline; actual publication has historically occurred in the days just before this deadline (e.g. Aug 27-29 in past years) or occasionally earlier

release_schedule.rule: A entidade competente do poder executivo federal fará publicar, no Diário Oficial da União, até o dia 31 de agosto de cada ano, a relação das populações dos Municípios (municipal estimates by Aug 31); state/Federal District estimates are published by Dec 31 of each year. Basis: Lei Complementar nº 143/2013 and Art. 102 of Lei nº 8.443/1992. Reference date for all estimates is July 1 of the respective year.
release_schedule.note: IBGE publishes 'Estimativas da População' annually. By law (Lei Complementar 143/2013; Lei 8.443/1992 Art. 102), municipal-level estimates must be released via Diário Oficial da União by August 31 each year, with July 1 as the reference date; state/UF-level estimates follow by Dec 31. Historical municipal releases: Aug 29, 2024; Aug 28, 2025 (per anda.ibge.gov.br). The 2026 edition, however, was reportedly released as early as July 1, 2026 (per press coverage), i.e. already published before today (2026-08-11), so the next expected edition is the 2027 one, due by the Aug 31, 2027 statutory deadline. No official IBGE dated release calendar (with a specific day) for the 2027 edition was found as of this research.

reports.title: Projeções da População do Brasil e Unidades da Federação
reports.publisher: Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE)
reports.description: IBGE's national and state-level population projections, issued in numbered revisions rather than annually. Named by exact title and revision in the Estimativas methodology note as one of the two inputs from which the municipal estimates are calculated. Revisão 2024 is the edition currently in use.
reports.cadence_note: Published as revisions — Revisão 2018, Revisão 2024 — rather than on a fixed schedule.

release_schedule.note: IBGE's own methodology documentation for this product states 'Periodicidade de divulgação: Eventual' (occasional/irregular release schedule), not a fixed annual or multi-year cadence. Revisions are published when new census/demographic data warrants an update: known past revisions were released in 2008, 2013, 2018, and most recently 22 August 2024 (Revisão 2024, based on the 2022 Census). IBGE states projections are 'monitoradas continuamente e passam por revisões periódicas' (continuously monitored and undergo periodic revisions) but gives no fixed schedule or announced date for the next revision.

reports.title: Lei nº 8.443, de 16 de julho de 1992 (Lei Orgânica do Tribunal de Contas da União)
reports.description: The TCU's organic law. Its art. 102, as replaced by Lei Complementar 143/2013, is the hinge of this whole slice: it obliges the competent federal executive entity to publish the population list in the Diário Oficial for the purposes of art. 1º VI — which is the TCU's own function of fixing the transfer coefficients. The original 1992 wording named the IBGE explicitly; the 2013 replacement generalised it to "entidade competente do Poder Executivo federal", and both texts remain visible in the consolidated version.
reports.cadence_note: A statute, amended rather than reissued.

release_schedule.note: Lei nº 8.443/1992 is the Organic Law of the Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) — a one-off foundational statute enacted by Congresso Nacional on 1992-07-16, published in the Diário Oficial da União and consolidated on Planalto's site (ccivil_03/leis/l8443.htm). It is not a recurring publication: there is no release calendar, no publisher-stated periodic rule, and no consistent annual/periodic pattern of new editions. Like other organic laws/codes, it is amended irregularly by subsequent legislation (leis ordinárias, leis complementares) whenever Congress acts, with no fixed cadence. releases_per_year=0.1 on file (implying roughly one 'release' per decade) is a rough proxy for irregular amendment frequency but should not be read as a real periodicity; recommend flagging this field as not meaningfully applicable to a foundational statute.

reports.title: Manual de Contabilidade Aplicada ao Setor Público (MCASP)
reports.description: Brazil's own national public-sector accounting manual, prescribing the accrual-basis Normas Brasileiras de Contabilidade Aplicadas ao Setor Público (NBC TSP) that federal, state and municipal entities follow. Its own text (Section 1, Contextualização) states the standards 'buscam a convergência às normas internacionais de contabilidade aplicada ao setor público – International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)' -- convergent-by-design, not identical-to. Currently in its 11th edition (effective 2025).
reports.cadence_note: Not stated as a fixed periodicity by STN. Estimated, not stated -- same convention Thomas approved for the German GNI/QNA inventories (Q2, Open-Questions-2026-08-08-sweep.docx) -- from four dated editions found live 2026-08-09 via Tesouro Transparente's own publication URLs: the 8th edition (2018-12-18), a 2021-11-08 edition, a 2023-12-22 edition, and the current 11th edition (2024-12-23). The three most recent editions are one year apart; earlier gaps were longer, so 1/yr is a recent-cadence estimate, not a demonstrated long-run average.

entries.covers: projected 12th edition, following the observed December-release pattern

release_schedule.note: STN has published new MCASP editions in December for the last two cycles (10th ed.: Dec 2023, effective Jan 2024; 11th ed.: Dec 2024, effective Jan 2025), each taking effect the following January. Earlier history is less regular (editions in Nov 2010, Jun 2011, Jul 2012, Dec 2014, Dec 2016, Dec 2018, Nov 2021 — gaps of 1-3 years), so the December cadence is only a recent trend, not a codified rule. As of 2026-08-11 I found no confirmation that a 12th edition was released in Dec 2025 (the gov.br manual page's most recent listed edition is still the 11th, Dec 2024, though the page metadata shows 'Publicado em 30/10/2025' which appears to be a content refresh, not a new edition). The Dec 2026 entry is a projection based on the pattern, not a confirmed date.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY, and minted on a three-document chain because NO SINGLE DOCUMENT STATES IT — the same treatment this corpus gave the New Zealand rating chain, where four statutory hops carry one edge. Stated plainly so a reader can judge it. (1) The decision itself, read via Wayback `id_` replay of the TCU's own PDF after portal.tcu.gov.br served a bot challenge, art. 1º: "Ficam aprovados, para o exercício de 2026, na forma dos Anexos I a X desta Decisão Normativa, os coeficientes individuais de participação no Fundo de Participação dos Municípios (FPM), previsto no art. 159, inciso I, alíneas “b”, “d”, “e” e “f”, da Constituição Federal, incluindo a Reserva instituída pelo art. 2º do Decreto-Lei 1.881, de 27 de agosto de 1981." (2) Its annexes, twenty-eight times, head the population column "População (fonte: IBGE, ref. 01/07/2025)" — AGENCY ONLY, plus a reference date that is the Estimativas release's own. (3) Lei 8.443/1992 art. 102 obliges publication of the population list "para os fins previstos no inciso VI do art. 1º desta Lei", art. 1º VI being the TCU's coefficient-fixing function. (4) IBGE's Estimativas methodology note closes it from the producer's side: "A partir de 1992, o IBGE passa a publicar no Diário Oficial da União - DOU, as Estimativas da População dos Municípios e Estados, em cumprimento ao Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, de 16.07.1992, para os fins previstos no inciso VI do Art. 1º da Lei nº 8.443." The relationship is documented; it is simply distributed across a decision, a statute and a methodology note rather than asserted in any one of them.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY (Nota metodológica n. 01 downloaded from biblioteca.ibge.gov.br with plain curl, 23 pages, pypdf-extracted). "As Estimativas da População residente nos Municípios, com data de referência em 1º de julho de 2025, foram calculadas com base nas Projeções da População do Brasil e Unidades da Federação, Revisão 2024, e nos totais populacionais dos Municípios enumerados pelos Censos Demográficos 2010 e 2022." Named by exact title AND revision — the strongest form of citation this corpus records, and notably stronger than anything in the decision that consumes the result.
dependencies.evidence_quote: As Estimativas da População residente nos Municípios, com data de referência em 1º de julho de 2025, foram calculadas com base nas Projeções da População do Brasil e Unidades da Federação, Revisão 2024, e nos totais populacionais dos Municípios enumerados pelos Censos Demográficos 2010 e 2022.

dependencies.basis: VERIFIED DIRECTLY (same methodology note, same sentence): "...e nos totais populacionais dos Municípios enumerados pelos Censos Demográficos 2010 e 2022." The note continues, on how the two censuses are used: "As populações recenseadas nos Municípios nesses dois últimos Censos Demográficos foram ajustadas e serviram de base para o estabelecimento da tendência de crescimento da população para as Estimativas da População até a data de referência, em 1º de julho de 2025." Two named censuses supplying a growth trend, not merely a benchmark.

VERIFIED DIRECTLY (methodology note, and the statute independently from planalto.gov.br). The note: "A partir de 1992, o IBGE passa a publicar no Diário Oficial da União - DOU, as Estimativas da População dos Municípios e Estados, em cumprimento ao Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, de 16.07.1992... Em 2013, foi publicada a Lei Complementar nº 143, de 17.07.2013, que altera o Art. 102 da Lei nº 8.443, estabelecendo que entidade competente do Poder Executivo Federal fará publicar no DOU, até o dia 31 de agosto de cada ano, a relação das populações dos Municípios..." The statute's own current text confirms it: "Art. 102. Entidade competente do Poder Executivo federal fará publicar no Diário Oficial da União, para os fins previstos no inciso VI do art. 1º desta Lei, a relação das populações: I - até 31 de dezembro de cada ano, no caso dos Estados e do Distrito Federal; II - até 31 de agosto de cada ano, no caso dos Municípios." `cites` rather than `methodology_depends_on`: the Act compels the publication and fixes its deadline, and supplies no method.

MCASP's own text (Section 1, Contextualização; 11th edition, effective 2025), quoted via a live-fetched public-sector-accounting reference source reproducing the manual: 'buscam a convergência às normas internacionais de contabilidade aplicada ao setor público – International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)'. Live-verified 2026-08-09.

_dropped.edge: br-fpm-dn-tcu -> a titled IBGE release, named in the decision itself
_dropped.why: THE HEADLINE NEGATIVE OF THIS SLICE, and the reason it was worth building. Research Brief XI asked whether the Decisão Normativa names an IBGE publication by title — a Portaria, an 'Estimativas da População' release — or only names the agency. VERIFIED DIRECTLY across all 206 pages: it names the agency. Every population column in every annex is headed "População (fonte: IBGE, ref. 01/07/2025)", twenty-eight occurrences, and the operative articles cite the Constitution, Decreto-Lei 1.881/1981, and the Leis Complementares 91/1997, 106/2001, 165/2019 and 198/2023 — statutes throughout, and not one publication. Brazil's FPM is plausibly the largest single application anywhere of the shape this corpus is built around: a formula dividing money among some five and a half thousand jurisdictions by a published statistical figure. And the formula document sources that figure the way the Local Government (Financial Assistance) Act 1995 (Cth) sources Australia's, and the Local Government (Financial Reporting and Prudence) Regulations 2014 source New Zealand's — by naming the statistician and not the statistic. The pattern now has instances on three continents.

VERIFIED AND MINTED 2026-08-09 (dropped-sweep, long tail). The homepage-only citation problem is fixed: the current manual is the 11th edition (STN, effective 2025, published 2024-12-23, live-fetched at gov.br/tesouronacional), and its own text -- quoted independently this session via a specialist public-sector-accounting reference site reproducing the manual's Section 1 (Contextualização), not re-derived from the original handoff's claim -- reads: 'buscam a convergência às normas internacionais de contabilidade aplicada ao setor público – International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS)', matching the handoff's transcription almost verbatim. Minted as br-mcasp (Manual de Contabilidade Aplicada ao Setor Público), edge methodology_depends_on -> ipsas (international-frameworks.json). This makes Brazil the largest IPSAS-convergent jurisdiction in the corpus by population, and settles the comparison this entry flagged as live: convergent-by-design (Brazil, alongside the Cook Islands' explicit adoption), not identical-to (no jurisdiction in this corpus states outright IPSAS adoption without qualification), and distinct from the Compact states' US GAAP basis and Niue's undocumented basis. Original text follows for history: NOT VERIFIED, and not minted for that reason. The submitted research reported, from the Manual de Contabilidade Aplicada ao Setor Público, that Brazilian public-sector standards "buscam a convergência às normas internacionais de contabilidade aplicada ao setor público – International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) – editadas pelo International Public Sector Accounting Standards Board (IPSASB)". The quote reads plausibly and the underlying fact is well known, but the entry cited `https://www.gov.br/tesouronacional/` — a homepage, not a document — so there is nothing to re-read. HIGH VALUE IF CLOSED: Brazil would be by far the largest IPSAS-convergent jurisdiction in this corpus, and the comparison against the Cook Islands (IPSAS by name and number), Greenland (its own statute), the Compact states (US GAAP) and Niue (nothing at all) is the live question of this whole branch. Needs the actual MCASP PDF and its edition.

_dropped.why: NOT VERIFIED. Reported as citing "o disposto no art. 165, § 3º, da Constituição da República Federativa do Brasil de 1988, e nos artigos 2º, 52 e 53, todos da Lei Complementar n° 101, de 4 de maio de 2000", which would make it a statutory bimonthly report under the Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal. Cited to `https://www.tesourotransparente.gov.br/` — again a portal rather than a document. The RREO is the obvious next Brazilian node and every federative entity produces one, which makes it the natural counterpart of `nz-la-annual-reports` and `au-la-annual-statements`. VERIFIED DIRECTLY 2026-08-09 (dropped-sweep, long tail), replacing the portal-only citation: LC 101/2000 (Lei de Responsabilidade Fiscal) Article 52 caput, live-quoted via a public-sector-accounting reference source reproducing the statute -- the RREO 'abrangerá todos os Poderes e o Ministério Público, será publicado até trinta dias após o encerramento de cada bimestre', explicitly tied to Article 165 §3 of the Constitution; Article 53 lists the accompanying statements. This confirms the claim is a real statutory bimonthly report, not a plausible-sounding portal blurb. MINTED 2026-08-09, in the dedicated Brazilian-fiscal-reporting session this entry called for: br-rreo, alongside a proper br-lc-101-2000 node and its RGF companion (br-rgf), all in the new file `src/data/research/br-fiscal-responsibility-law.json`. Kept out of this file rather than added here, since the FPM chain still has no documented dependency on or from the RREO/RGF chain -- the two are separate slices sharing only the same governing statute's country, not an edge. See that file for the full Art. 52/53/54/55 quotations and the methodology_depends_on edges to br-lc-101-2000.

_dropped.edge: The Estimativas da População release page's own statement of legal purpose
_dropped.why: A sourcing note, recorded because it is the third instance of one pattern. The submitted research quoted an IBGE sentence beginning "Atendendo ao dispositivo legal, Lei nº 8443, de 16 de julho de 1992, no artigo 102..." and attributed it to the Estimativas programme page. That sentence could not be located: `www.ibge.gov.br` returns HTTP 403 to ordinary requests, and the Wayback copy of the page does not contain it either. It is not used. Its claim is nonetheless fully established by the methodology note, which was read directly and says the same thing at greater length. The pattern — an unlocatable sentence displacing better text that was sitting in the same set of documents — has now occurred with the Marshall Islands Single Audit requirement, the Palau audit mandate, and here.
